entry.name: seq
entry.digest: Sequencer for recording and playing MIDI data
entry.description: seq is a sequencer of raw MIDI bytes. You can control the speed of playback (only at the time you start it), read and write from files, and record from live MIDI input. See also midiparse and midiformat which you may need to get to and from raw MIDI.

attributes.digest: Override Sequence Tempo
attributes.description: If enabled (default =(disabled)), the value of theattribute will override any tempo requested by the sequence. In this case,attribute will not be updated when a new file is read, nor when tempo meta messages appear in the sequence data. The meta messages will continue to be output from the right outlet of theobject in this case.

attributes.digest: Playback Tempo
attributes.description: If thehas read a MIDI file with tempo information, theattribute will reflect the current tempo at the current playback time. If the file has no tempo information, the default tempo is 120. (120 BPM). Theattribute can be modified to change the playback speed, but will be overwritten by tempo changes present in the MIDI file, and will be overwritten when a new MIDI file is read.

messages.name: addeventdelay
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, adds to theonset time, in milliseconds, of the first event in the recorded sequence.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, adds to theonset time, in milliseconds, of the first event in the recorded sequence. All events in the sequence are shifted so that the first event occurs at the specified onset time.

messages.name: append
messages.digest: Starts recording at the end of the stored sequence, without erasing the existing sequence.
messages.description: Starts recording at the end of the stored sequence, without erasing the existing sequence.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Starts playing the sequence stored in.
messages.description: Starts playing the sequence stored in.

messages.name: clear
messages.description: Clears the sequence currently stored in theobject.

messages.name: delay
messages.digest: The word, followed by a number, sets the onset time, in milliseconds, of the first event in the recorded sequence.
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the onset time, in milliseconds, of the first event in the recorded sequence. All events in the sequence are shifted so that the first event occurs at the specified onset time.

messages.name: dump
messages.digest: Opens a standard Open Document dialog box, to select a saved sequence or standard MIDI file.
messages.description: Opens a standard Open Document dialog box, to select a saved sequence or standard MIDI file. The selected file is opened as text in a new Untitled text window, which can be edited and saved.

messages.name: hook
messages.digest: The word, followed by a float, multiplies all the event times in the stored sequence by that number.
messages.description: The word, followed by a float, multiplies all the event times in the stored sequence by that number. For example, if the number is 2.0, all event times will be doubled, and the sequence will play back twice as slowly. Multiplications can even be performed while the sequence is playing.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Whenis recording, numbers received in its inlet are interpreted as bytes of MIDI messages (usually fromor).
messages.description: Whenis recording, numbers received in its inlet are interpreted as bytes of MIDI messages (usually fromor). MIDI channel messages and system exclusive messages can be recorded by, butdoes not respond directly to MIDI real time messages such as start, stop, MIDI clock, etc.

messages.name: print
messages.digest: Prints the first sixteen events of the recorded sequence in the Max Console.
messages.description: Prints the first sixteen events of the recorded sequence in the Max Console.

messages.name: read
messages.digest: With no arguments,calls up the standard Open Document dialog box, so that a previously recorded sequence can be read into, replacing the current sequence. With a symbol as an argument,searches for a file with the specified name to read into theobject.Note: Theobject reads and writes both single track (format 0) and multi-track (format 1) standard MIDI files.
messages.description: With no arguments,calls up the standard Open Document dialog box, so that a previously recorded sequence can be read into, replacing the current sequence. With a symbol as an argument,searches for a file with the specified name to read into theobject.Note: Theobject reads and writes both single track (format 0) and multi-track (format 1) standard MIDI files. It can also read and write text files in which each line consists of a start time in milliseconds (the time elapsed since the beginning of the sequence) followed by the (space-separated) bytes of a MIDI message recorded at that start time. For example,0 144 60 112;1000 144 60 0;1500 192 31;1500 144 60 112;2500 144 60 0;plays the note middle C on channel 1 for one second, then half a second later changes to program number 31 and plays middle C again for one second.

messages.name: record
messages.digest: Starts recording MIDI messages received in the inlet.
messages.description: Starts recording MIDI messages received in the inlet.

messages.name: start
messages.digest: The wordby itself has the same effect as.
messages.description: The wordby itself has the same effect as. The word, followed by a number, plays the stored sequence at a tempo determined by the number. The messageindicates normal tempo. If the number is,plays the sequence at half the original recorded speed,plays it back at twice the original speed, and so on.The messagestarts the sequencer, but rather than follow Max's millisecond clock,waits for amessage to advance its clock. See themessage.

messages.name: stop
messages.digest: Stops the sequencer if it is recording or playing.
messages.description: Stops the sequencer if it is recording or playing. Amessage need not be received when switching directly from playing to recording, or vice-versa.

messages.name: tick
messages.digest: Afterhas received amessage, it waits formessages to advance its clock. In order to play the sequence at its original recorded tempo,must receive 48messages per second. This is equivalent to 24s per quarter note (the standard for a MIDI Clock message)
messages.description: Afterhas received amessage, it waits formessages to advance its clock. In order to play the sequence at its original recorded tempo,must receive 48messages per second. This is equivalent to 24s per quarter note (the standard for a MIDI Clock message) at a tempo of 120MM. By usingmessages to advance the sequencer, you can vary the tempo of playback or synchronizewith another timing source (such as incoming MIDI Clock messages).

messages.name: write
messages.digest: Calls up the standard Save As dialog box, so that a recorded sequence can be saved as a separate file.
messages.description: Calls up the standard Save As dialog box, so that a recorded sequence can be saved as a separate file. If you want to edit the sequence with the text editor, check the Save As Text option in the dialog box. With a symbol as an argument,will write a file with the specified name. A non-zero int argument (as a single argument, or following a filename argument) will cause theobject to write a multi-track standard MIDI file (format 1).
